name: thin-results
about: Results exist but each rests on one or two leads: too thin to steer by.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook straight_talk (straight talk) and scene cab_pov (from the cab) spent $41.20 in the last 28 days over 3010 impressions and brought 1 lead, $41.20 per lead.
Our ads with hook proof (proof) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $38.75 in the last 28 days over 2890 impressions and brought 2 leads, $19.38 per lead.

output.audience: Class A drivers who meet the experience requirement and run flatbed or regional freight in the Midwest now, often in a larger fleet. They want weekly home time and a truck that is theirs. A plain pay per mile and a small fleet where dispatch knows them would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile for regional flatbed work, shown over a loaded flatbed moving on a Midwest highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay is the clearest fact of this job and drivers compare it directly. This hook and scene have not been measured here, so treat it as a test.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, shown as a quiet home street at the end of a regional week.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on regional Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Home time is what separates regional work from longer runs. No earlier ad of ours has led with it, so nothing is measured.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck, shown as a flatbed rig parked and waiting for its own driver.
angles.proof: The job gives an assigned truck and the work is flatbed.
angles.why: An assigned truck matters to drivers who share equipment now. The truck-at-rest scene had our lower cost per lead under another hook, but over very few leads, so it is thin.

angles.idea: State plainly who this is for: Class A flatbed drivers who meet the experience requirement and run Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The opening states an experience requirement, flatbed work and Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Naming the requirement and the area up front keeps unqualified or out-of-area drivers from applying. Our earlier ad of this kind brought very few leads at a higher cost, so that result is thin.

angles.idea: Lead with the terms as plain proof: the pay per mile, the retirement plan, and a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: The opening states pay per mile and a retirement plan, in a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.why: A proof hook had our lower cost per lead in earlier ads, with a different picture and over very few leads, so it is thin. The stated terms give it facts to show.
